figures.claim: A rigid body in space has six degrees of freedom: it can rotate about three axes and translate along three.

Conventional teaching gives flexion and extension about 140 degrees, axial rotation up to about 30 degrees at 90 degrees of flexion, varus and valgus a few degrees, anteroposterior translation about 5 to 10 mm, and medial to lateral translation and compression to distraction one or two millimetres each.
